coverage.completionBoundary: Adoption and completion of this portfolio would prove that the selected StarCraft API scope has a ratified authority contract, repository implementation, automated tests, bounded local security and recovery behavior, exact-source Windows packaging, and the declared acceptance evidence. Source and local tests prove at most IMPLEMENTED or TESTED. VERIFIED requires clean-Windows genuine-replay observation; USED requires owner usage evidence. This portfolio would not prove live battlefield truth, coaching correctness, player improvement, Battle.net service availability, public deployment, commercial readiness, or implementation of the complete Strategy Science backlog.
exclusions: No browser-direct Battle.net or Blizzard web API calls.
No external credentials, OAuth flow, background network traffic, or cloud service until an explicit opt-in decision is ratified.
No live StarCraft process telemetry, memory inspection, input automation, bot behavior, or claim of unreported battlefield truth.
No mutation or replacement of Strategic OS, player-report authority, or the canonical browser event log.
No implementation of the complete Python Strategy Science program.
No redistribution of Blizzard artwork, game assets, binaries, or proprietary data.
No public release, commercial-readiness, customer, revenue, or launch requirements for this personal application.
No automatic lifecycle promotion, backlog adoption, deployment claim, player-use claim, or improvement-outcome claim.
journeys: Player launches the local or packaged Master Intel application and sees whether the installed StarCraft II API renderer is available.
Player imports or selects a trusted local replay and explicitly selects their replay-player identity.
Player requests an API-rendered replay moment from the replay review surface.
The loopback service validates case identity, replay integrity, player identity, timestamp, patch, BaseBuild, and bounded request parameters.
The installed StarCraft II engine renders player-POV and observer-truth frames without promoting observer truth into the player's historical knowledge.
Master Intel presents the rendered evidence, provenance, uncertainty, and one bounded continuation into practice.

Missing game installation, missing matching BaseBuild, corrupt replay, unsupported protocol, unavailable graphics, timeout, cancellation, and stale cached capture each produce a truthful recovery route.
Keyboard, screen-reader, reduced-motion, narrow-width, zoom, loading, error, retry, and cancellation states remain usable.
Private exact-SHA Windows packaging preserves protocol dependencies and produces an acceptance candidate.
A named owner completes a clean-Windows genuine-replay acceptance run before VERIFIED or USED claims are considered.

sourcesReviewed.finding: Requires Canonical Project State reconciliation, preserves Strategic OS and player reports as live authority, keeps Python advisory, and limits lifecycle claims to their evidence.
Requires immutable snapshots, advisory proof-carrying Python output, patch matching, deterministic fallback, bounded local workers, and no direct mutation of Strategic OS state.

Establishes Strategic OS authority, offline-first loopback-only operation, Master Intel as the primary shell, replay-integrity controls, patched protocol compatibility, and private exact-SHA Windows acceptance.
Defines the replay-to-practice primary journey, player-report-driven Guided Execution, current API and replay capabilities, unresolved clean-Windows proof, and PROOF-NEXT-001.
States that Master Intel is the primary product shell, replay analysis is postgame, live battlefield truth comes from player reports, and the app does not read the live StarCraft process.
Indexes the canonical machine ledger, evidence registers, existing Python Strategy Science backlog, architecture, contracts, schemas, and acceptance coverage.
Confirms Python Strategy Science is advisory, dependency-light, and only partially operationalized; most planned capabilities are not active application features.
Runs project-state validation for pull requests and pushes to main or v1.13-dev, but does not explicitly include the personal/v1.14.0-candidate branch in push triggers.
Registers sc2reader as TESTED, PySC2 and installed-SC2 frame capture as IMPLEMENTED, the SC2 replay frame-capture boundary as TESTED, and successful clean-Windows capture as UNVERIFIED.
Already uses PySC2 and s2clientprotocol to select the replay-matched local SC2 build and render player-POV and observer-truth replay frames with explicit evidence boundaries.
Already exposes capture readiness, synchronous replay-frame capture, frame serving, bounded timestamp validation, and explicit unavailable and reconstruction-fallback responses.
Current focused capture coverage verifies only safe output naming and does not exercise the complete capture adapter or Flask journey.
Verifies the patched protobuf pin, s2clientprotocol imports, exact BaseBuild selection, Windows runtime discovery, and release-version consistency.
Defines local API error contracts, performance budgets, feature flags, evidence classes, diagnostics, cancellation, privacy requirements, and optional-network gating.
Contains the broader Strategy Science program; this proposed integration portfolio must be reconciled into that authority rather than becoming a second canonical backlog.

unresolvedQuestions: Does StarCraft API mean the already-integrated local PySC2 and s2clientprotocol replay-rendering API, Blizzard Battle.net profile and game-data APIs, a live SC2 client API, or a governed combination?
Is the intended outcome postgame replay evidence only, or does the owner want live observations that would require explicitly revisiting the current player-report and no-live-process boundary?
If Battle.net web data is required, which endpoints, regions, account scopes, consent model, credentials, rate limits, terms, retention rules, and offline fallback are authorized?
How should any newly admitted API data be classified among game_rule, replay_fact, source_claim, inference, simulation, and hypothesis?
Which Windows versions, StarCraft II patches, replay BaseBuilds, graphics configurations, and installation layouts are supported?
Should personal/v1.14.0-candidate receive direct push-triggered project-state CI coverage, or remain governed through pull-request and manually dispatched workflows?
What timeout and concurrency limits are acceptable when the installed game briefly launches to render frames?
Who is the named human acceptance owner, and which consented genuine replay may be used for clean-Windows proof?
What Blizzard terms, API policies, trademark rules, and redistribution constraints must be reviewed if the scope expands beyond local installed-game replay rendering?
